alphabet_grammar.name: Alphabet Grammar
alphabet_grammar.description: One generative rule, one stream of 144 seeded numbers, seven symbol sets, and the number of symbols turns out to predict nothing. A 0.96 x 0.96 x 0.16 m loom frame carries a 0.84 m square raster of 12 x 12 cells; every alphabet reads THE SAME 144 draws, so the symbol set is the only thing that differs between any two cells. Two artifacts and three names declare an axis called alphabet - GeneticProgramming and genetic_programming are ONE SCENE under two registry names, confirmed by identical scene paths, differing only in that one fixtures a population_seed and the other does not. The brief said 10 PRINT's alphabet is two characters, a CSG tree's is a handful of booleans on solids, and a voxel alphabet is one cube. All three are wrong about this code. ten_print_textile's alphabet axis never changes the SIZE at all: diagonals, orthogonals and blocks are three TWO-symbol alphabets, one fair coin, three unrecognisably different cloths. voxel is not one cube: create_voxel_genome writes a cube where randf() < 0.3, so the alphabet is cube-and-VOID and the void does half the work. And csg_tree has the biggest declared alphabet in the family - three operations by three solids, nine gene kinds - and draws ONE MARK, because add_primitive_to_surface reads the operation into a local variable, ignores it, ignores the primitive, and emits three vertices of a cube: one flat right triangle, for all nine. The reach reading measures it: collect every distinct 2 x 2 neighbourhood of the field, keyed by WHAT IS DRAWN rather than what was declared, and stand each one on its own plaque. Sixteen plaques for every two-symbol alphabet, about 96 for four, 121 for the continuum - and ONE for the nine-symbol alphabet. Deterministic from seed 20260816. No randf outside it, no noise, no _process, no Timer.
dev_themes: the vocabulary is not the reach
a synonym is not a symbol
interactions: read the glyphs row across the alphabet axis and then read the reach shelf across the same axis. glyphs ranks csg_tree first with nine plaques and diagonals last with two; reach reverses it exactly - one plaque against sixteen. Those two rows are the whole argument and they are the same seven alphabets

stand at csg_tree, reading=reach. ONE plaque. Nine declared symbols, one drawn mark, and every gate in this project passes the declaration, because the enum is honest and the collapse happens in the renderer

compare diagonals and orthogonals in the field reading. Same 144 draws, same 144 symbol indices, same bar, same two colours - the ONLY difference in the whole frame is that one pair of rotations is +-45 degrees and the other is 0 and 90. One reads as a maze and the other as a rib

look for the second symbol of voxel. It is not there, and it is a symbol: the empty cell is what makes 2^512 bodies out of one cube. In the glyphs reading it is the bare plaque, which is the most honest object in the sheet

put parametric beside blocks in the reach reading: a shelf saturated at 121 against a shelf at 16. Then notice the shelf cannot go past 121, so a continuum and a 256-symbol alphabet are indistinguishable to it - the instrument is censored by its own sample and says so
alphabet_grammar.capacity: SEE that an alphabet's SIZE is a fact about its declaration and its REACH is a fact about what renders, and that the two can point in opposite directions - nine symbols reaching one configuration while two symbols reach sixteen

spatial_needs.footprint_note: THE LOOM FRAME IS THE FOOTPRINT AND IT IS DRAWN BEFORE EITHER AXIS IS CONSULTED: two uprights 0.045 x 0.96 x 0.16 at x = +-0.4575, two beams 0.96 x 0.045 x 0.16 at y = 0.0225 and 0.9375, and a solid back 0.90 x 0.90 x 0.08 behind them. The world box is 0.96 x 0.96 x 0.16 in all twenty-one cells before a single mark exists. Without the frame the box would be a fact about which alphabet was picked - primitives reach 0.064 m forward and the textile bars only 0.017, csg_tree's triangle is a plane with no thickness at all, and the reach shelf at csg_tree is ONE plaque 0.070 m square against parametric's 121. The camera would move between cells and every measured pair would carry a framing difference it did not earn. The FIGURE inside the frame moves enormously: 144 marks under field, two plaques under glyphs at any two-symbol alphabet, nine under glyphs at csg_tree, one under reach at csg_tree and 121 under reach at parametric. THE PANEL IS VERTICAL, which is not a style choice: at capture_config_sweep's standpoint a horizontal plane projects at 0.084 of its area and a vertical one in the xy plane at 0.787, nine times better, and ten_print_textile's cloth is already a hanging bolt. layout=ladder stands all seven alphabets in a row at 1.10 m pitch, about 7.6 m wide, and is a design view rather than a map placement.

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry in a Python replica built from the same constants; no Godot was run. The box is the FRAME and nothing else: the uprights span x at +-0.48 and y from 0 to 0.96 at a depth of 0.16, and nothing either axis draws can exceed them. The deepest thing any alphabet builds is a primitives glyph, whose 0.063 m box sits on a 0.008 m plaque 0.001 m off the backing and tops out at z = 0.072 against the frame's 0.080; the widest is the reach shelf, 11 columns at 0.0763636 m = 0.84 m inside a 0.90 m backing; the tallest is the same shelf at 11 rows.

dna.default: alphabet=diagonals, reading=field. diagonals because IT IS THE ONLY VALUE IN THE UNION THAT IS ALSO ITS OWN MEMBER'S SHIPPED DEFAULT - ten_print_textile.gd:22 declares `var alphabet: String = "diagonals"` and that member's registry `default` line says why: it returns the same box at the same rotation.z = +-PI*0.25, so all seven of its live placements weave exactly the cloth they wove before. GeneticProgramming's default is `primitives`, which its own header calls the legacy lineage rather than a claim, and picking it would have made the flagship cell the one whose marks are four Godot mesh primitives with no argument in them. field because it is the only reading BOTH members actually build: GeneticProgramming's visualize_population lays the population out and ten_print_textile's _build weaves the bolt; neither has ever drawn its own vocabulary or its own reach, which is what the other two readings are for. NOTE WHAT THE DEFAULT CELL COSTS: it is the plainest tile in the sheet - the shipped cloth, the thing 10 PRINT already looks like - and it is deliberately the reference the other six alphabets are read against rather than an argument on its own. That would normally be a bad place to solve framing on, except that framing here is set by the loom frame and the frame is identical in all twenty-one cells.
dna.note:
WHAT THE VALUES MEAN, where each came from, and the symbol count of each - because that number is this artifact's subject.

THE FAMILY FIRST, AND IT IS A CENSUS BEFORE IT IS AN ARGUMENT. Three registry names declare an axis called `alphabet`. TWO OF THEM ARE ONE SCENE. GeneticProgramming and genetic_programming both sit in commons/artifacts/registry/procgen_extra.json and both name the identical scene, res://algorithms/proceduralgeneration/growth_systems/genetic_programming/GeneticProgramming.tscn; that directory holds exactly one script carrying the axis. They declare the same four values in the same order and the same second axis `muster`, and they differ in bookkeeping only: one says category `unknown` / complexity `beginner` and carries dna.fixture {"population_seed": 20260802}, the other says `procedural` / `advanced` and carries NO fixture at all. So the same scene is registered once as seeded and once as unseeded, which means one of the two names sweeps a population Godot randomises at boot. That is the eighth confirmation of the one-scene-many-names pattern in this programme, and the tell was the identical export list.

A SECOND FACT ABOUT THAT SCENE, because it changes what the source's axis IS. GeneticProgramming.tscn's ROOT is a scriptless Node3D and the script hangs on a CHILD also called GeneticProgramming. GridInteractablesComponent sets config_* metadata and calls apply_grid_config on the ROOT, so a map token's config_alphabet never reaches _read_dna_meta. The axis is reachable from the sweep, which sets the property directly, and from the editor. It has never been reachable from a map placement. Nothing here depends on that; a reader comparing this bench to its source should know.

AND ten_print_textile SAYS OUT LOUD WHERE ITS WORD CAME FROM. Its registry `vocabulary_note` reads: "alphabet is taken from GeneticProgramming.alphabet - the symbol set a generator draws from - which is precisely the question here." So this is not a coincidence of naming across two domains. One member borrowed the other's word on purpose, and this bench is the room where the two vocabularies are finally put in the same frame.

THE THING THE CODE SAYS THAT THE BRIEF DID NOT, AND IT IS THE FINDING - three corrections, in ascending order of how much they matter.

  ONE. ten_print_textile's `alphabet` AXIS NEVER CHANGES THE ALPHABET'S SIZE. All three of its values are TWO-symbol alphabets. The brief guessed `diagonals` was the two slashes and was right - it is the +-45 degree bar, the PETSCII pair of `10 PRINT CHR$(205.5+RND(1)); : GOTO 10`, drawn as a rotated box rather than as a character. It then asked what `orthogonals` and `blocks` are. They are TWO MORE PAIRS. `orthogonals` is _mark's second branch and its own comment says it: "the same flip, a different alphabet: a lying bar and a standing one" - THE SAME BOX at rotation.z 0.0 and PI*0.5. `blocks` is _mark's first branch: "No line at all: the flip read as a bitmap" - a filled cell 0.9 of the cell square against a speck 0.3 of it. One fair coin, three pairs of marks, three cloths that do not look remotely alike. THE MEMBER'S OWN AXIS IS ALREADY THE EXPERIMENT the brief wanted this bench to run, and whoever wrote it had the finding first.

  TWO. `voxel` IS NOT ONE CUBE. create_voxel_genome walks an 8 x 8 x 8 grid and appends a voxel where `randf() < 0.3`. The alphabet is {cube, VOID} and the void is doing half the work: with one symbol and a random rule you get exactly one picture and no reach at all, and it is the empty cell beside the cube that makes 2^512 bodies out of 512 slots. Everything the brief credited to "one cube, given enough of them" belongs to the symbol that draws nothing. The count is TWO.

  THREE, AND IT IS THE ONE WORTH THE PASS. `csg_tree` HAS THE LARGEST DECLARED ALPHABET IN THE FAMILY AND DRAWS ONE MARK. create_csg_genome rolls an operation from {union, subtract, intersect} and a primitive from {sphere, box, cylinder}: nine distinct gene kinds. Then build_csg_phenotype hands each gene to add_primitive_to_surface, which reads the operation into a local variable, never uses it, never looks at the primitive either, builds an eight-corner vertex list and adds THREE OF THEM - vertices[0], [1], [2], the lower-left half of one cube face. Nine words, one flat right triangle. Two further consequences fall out of the same line and are worth recording: because Gene.gene_type is set to the OPERATION name, estimate_volume's match on "sphere"/"box"/"cylinder" never fires, so every csg genome has volume 0 and the default fitness function ranks them all identically; and Gene.mutate's match never fires either, so csg genes never mutate their parameters. The branch is inert at three levels and the axis declaration is honest about none of it, because the enum IS honest - all four values exist and all four are reachable. check_dna_declarations.py passes this axis. The collapse is one layer below anything the corpus's gates can see.

SO THE THESIS SOMEONE CAN DISAGREE WITH: an alphabet's SIZE is a fact about its declaration and its REACH is a fact about what renders, and the two can point in opposite directions. A symbol that draws what every other symbol draws is not a symbol, it is a synonym.


ALPHABET - SEVEN VALUES, and the count of each is written first because the count is the subject. THE SAME 144 DRAWS FEED ALL SEVEN. One RandomNumberGenerator seeded at 20260816 produces 144 uniform floats in row-major order, top row first, once per rebuild; the alphabet is nothing but the partition of [0,1) those floats are read through. No alphabet gets more randomness than another. The four two-symbol alphabets therefore receive THE SAME 144 SYMBOL INDICES, which is what makes any pair of them a pure test of the marks.

  diagonals    2 SYMBOLS - ten_print_textile. A bar CELL*0.9 = 0.063 m long and CELL*0.42 = 0.0294 m thick, at rotation.z = +PI/4 for the coin's heads and -PI/4 for tails. The shipped cloth and this bench's default. NOTE WHAT IS AND IS NOT REPRODUCED: 10 PRINT's maze reads as a maze because the PETSCII glyphs run corner to corner and join across cell boundaries. This bar is 0.9 of the cell, so at 45 degrees it reaches 0.636 of the cell in each direction and stops 0.032 m short of the corner. The marks nearly touch and do not. That is the source's geometry, kept, and it is why this cloth reads as diagonal dashes rather than as a continuous labyrinth.
  orthogonals  2 SYMBOLS - ten_print_textile. THE IDENTICAL BAR at rotation.z = 0.0 and PI*0.5. Same length, same thickness, same two colours, same 144 indices as `diagonals`. The only difference between those two cells in the entire sheet is 90 degrees of rotation applied to 144 objects, and it is the pre-registered closest pair for exactly that reason.
  blocks       2 SYMBOLS - ten_print_textile. A filled cell 0.063 m square against a speck 0.021 m square, both unrotated. The source's line: "No line at all: the flip read as a bitmap, filled cell vs speck." This is the value that shows a two-symbol alphabet producing no structure whatever - a dither, not a maze - under the same coin that produces the maze.
  voxel        2 SYMBOLS - GeneticProgramming. A cube 0.056 m on a side, which is CELL*0.8 because the source builds BoxMesh size 0.4 on a 0.5 lattice pitch; and a VOID, which draws nothing and is still a symbol. In the glyphs reading it is the bare plaque, and that bare plaque is the most honest object in the sheet.
  primitives   4 SYMBOLS - GeneticProgramming. sphere, box, cylinder, torus: the four strings in Genome.create_random_gene's `types` array, built with the four mesh classes build_primitive_phenotype builds them with, at that function's own proportions. INCLUDING ITS SQUASHED SPHERE: the source writes `sphere.radius = 0.5; sphere.height = sphere.radius`, so the bead is half as tall as it is wide, and that is kept rather than corrected. Each primitive is fitted to a 0.063 m maximum extent, preserving each mesh's own aspect (torus inner 0.3 / outer 0.7 becomes 0.0135 / 0.0315). The torus is stood up 90 degrees about x so its hole faces the camera; lying in xz the way TorusMesh builds it, a wall-mounted torus photographs as a line. All four wear ONE colour, Color(0.6, 0.7, 0.9), because build_primitive_phenotype gives every gene the same material - so this alphabet is told apart by SHAPE alone, which is the source's decision and not this bench's.
  csg_tree     9 DECLARED, 1 DRAWN - GeneticProgramming. {union, subtract, intersect} x {sphere, box, cylinder}. All nine arrive at add_primitive_to_surface and leave as the identical zero-thickness right triangle with 0.063 m legs. The triangle has no thickness because the source emits three vertices and nothing else; CULL_DISABLED carries it. 144 identical triangles in the field reading, nine identical triangles in the glyphs reading, ONE plaque in the reach reading.
  parametric   A CONTINUUM - GeneticProgramming. The draw IS the symbol: there is no partition and no K. One trig surface per cell from build_parametric_phenotype's own equation and its own three-vertex triangle pattern, at resolution 6 instead of 20, scaled into a 0.063 m box. The eight non-phase parameters are pinned at the midpoints of the source's own randf_range calls (amp 1.25 of 0.5..2.0, freq 1.75 of 0.5..3.0) so that exactly ONE number is spent per cell, as the rule requires; phase_x = phase_y = phase_z = u * TAU. At the generator's 32-bit precision the alphabet has 2^32 = 4.29 billion members, which is 2.1 billion times `diagonals`. WORTH NOTICING ABOUT THE SOURCE'S SURFACE: x depends on u only and y and z on v only, so it is a curve in (y, z) swept along x - a ribbon, not a closed body. That one alphabet cannot make a hole, cannot make a heap, and cannot make a corner, whatever its cardinality.

SO THE SIZE COLUMN READS 2, 2, 2, 2, 4, 9, 4294967296. Four of the seven are the same number.


READING - THREE VALUES, and two of them argue with each other.

  field   THE RULE RUN. 12 x 12 = 144 cells at 0.070 m over a 0.84 m square, one draw and one symbol each. What the alphabet makes. This is the only reading either source has ever built: GeneticProgramming's visualize_population arranges the population in a grid and ten_print_textile's _build weaves the bolt.
  glyphs  THE VOCABULARY ITSELF. One plaque 0.084 m square per symbol, evenly spaced at a 0.84/9 pitch and centred, with the symbol standing on it AT TRUE SIZE - the same dimensions it has in the field, not enlarged. Two plaques for each of the four two-symbol alphabets, four for primitives, nine for csg_tree, and nine SAMPLES for parametric, which has no finite vocabulary to lay out and whose sampled row is labelled as a sample here rather than passed off as complete. THE PLAQUE COUNT IS THE ALPHABET'S SIZE, STANDING UP AS MATTER, and this is the reading that makes the size claim visible. It is also the only reading that does not consume the stream: it enumerates the alphabet instead of sampling it, so the representative draw for symbol s of K is (s + 0.5)/K, the midpoint of that symbol's own share of [0,1). THE DRAWN AREAS, because a two-symbol row is the sparsest thing in the sheet and lesson (c) exists: two plaques at 0.007056 m2 each plus two marks at 0.0018522 m2 each is 0.0178 m2 of world surface, which projects to 1.45 percent of the subject box - about seven times the critic's blank floor of 0.2 percent. The nine-plaque row is 0.0708 m2, 5.8 percent. Nothing in this reading is near blank and the numbers are here so that can be checked rather than believed.
  reach   THE SPACE ACTUALLY SPANNED, and the reading that refutes `glyphs`. Every 2 x 2 neighbourhood of the field - 11 x 11 = 121 overlapping blocks - is keyed by WHAT ITS FOUR CELLS DRAW rather than by what was declared, and each DISTINCT key gets its own 0.070 m plaque on an 11-column shelf in first-occurrence order, carrying its four marks at half size. The shelf's occupancy is the number, built as matter, and 11 columns by 11 rows is exactly 121 so a saturated shelf fills the panel with nothing trimmed. MEASURED ON A PYTHON REPLICA OVER 400 INDEPENDENT STREAMS, before any capture:

    diagonals / orthogonals / blocks / voxel   16   (16 in 98.75 percent of streams, 15 in the rest)
    primitives                                 97   (range 85-107 over 400 streams; the independent-draw expectation is 256 x (1 - (255/256)^121) = 96.4)
    csg_tree                                    1   (exactly, in every stream, by construction)
    parametric                                121   (exactly, in every stream, by construction)

  THAT TABLE IS THE ARGUMENT IN ONE ROW. Sizes 2, 2, 2, 2, 4, 9, 4.29e9; reaches 16, 16, 16, 16, 97, 1, 121. The largest FINITE alphabet in the sheet has the smallest reach in the sheet, by two orders of magnitude, and the ranking by size and the ranking by reach are not merely different, they are inverted at the top.

THE HONEST LIMIT OF `reach`, WRITTEN DOWN RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER. 121 blocks can never exhibit more than 121 distinct configurations, so the shelf is CENSORED BY THE SAMPLE. It separates 1 from 16 from 97 cleanly and it CANNOT separate primitives' true 4^4 = 256 from parametric's continuum, because both saturate: primitives comes back at 97 only because 121 draws from 256 collide, not because its space is smaller. A full shelf means "at least 121", never "121". That is a real limit on the instrument and it is the dark spot of this artifact: the reading that refutes the size claim is itself unable to measure a large alphabet, which is why the case it settles is the one at the bottom - nine against one - and not the one at the top.


HOW THE SHEET IS PROTECTED FROM THE COLOUR TRAP. Every GeneticProgramming alphabet wears ONE colour, because the source hands each phenotype branch a single material: primitives Color(0.6, 0.7, 0.9), voxel (0.5, 0.8, 0.6), csg (0.8, 0.6, 0.4), parametric (0.9, 0.5, 0.7). All four are kept exactly. Only ten_print_textile colours by SYMBOL, warm hue 0.07 for heads and cool 0.58 for tails, and those two are the one place a source colour was altered - see `declines`. The full Rec.709 luminance ladder: backing 0.109, frame 0.211, plaque 0.310, cool 0.493, parametric 0.599, csg 0.628, primitives 0.693, warm 0.694, voxel 0.722. The three things that must be told apart INSIDE one frame - backing, plaque, mark - are 0.201 and 0.183 apart at the closest. Primitives at 0.693 and warm at 0.694 are a coincidence and a harmless one: they never appear in the same frame, and across frames the changed pixels are mark-against-backing at 0.58 separation, never mark-against-mark. If the critic's colour-only rescue ever fires on this sheet it is reporting a fault, not a rescue.

THE DISAGREEMENT AVAILABLE, and it is fair. A reader can say csg_tree's collapse is a BUG, that a bug is not a fact about alphabets, and that building a whole value out of a stub is scoring a point off a typo. Three answers. First, the stub is the alphabet as far as anything that renders is concerned, and "what renders" is the only definition of reachable set that a still can hold. Second, the source's own DNA header already declares the stub and keeps the value anyway - "a truthful tile of a stub is better than a hidden one" - so this bench is agreeing with it and measuring the consequence it did not state. Third and most importantly, the same collapse is available without any bug: `orthogonals` and `diagonals` have identical size, identical rule, identical draws and completely different fields, and `blocks` has the same size again and produces no structure at all. The thesis stands on the three-cell textile row alone. csg_tree is the extreme case, not the load-bearing one. THE CELL WHERE HOLDING THE THESIS COSTS SOMETHING is parametric under reach, where the honest instrument reports 121 and the true answer is 4.29 billion - the reading that refutes the size claim is silent about the largest alphabet in the sheet.

predicted_degeneracy.pair: diagonals against orthogonals, in the glyphs reading
predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic:
THE CONTEXT IS THE `glyphs` COLUMN AND THE RANKING IS COMPUTED INSIDE IT: twenty-one pairs over seven alphabets, and this is the floor of them. It is also the floor of the whole sheet, because `glyphs` is the sparsest reading - the same pair costs 16 x 4 = 64 half-size marks under `reach` and 144 full-size marks under `field`, which is 8x and 72x the changed area computed below.

WHY THIS PAIR IS THE FLOOR, AND IT IS BY CONSTRUCTION. Both alphabets have exactly two symbols, so both draw TWO PLAQUES at the identical two positions (x = -0.046667 and +0.046667, y = 0.48, 0.084 m square, 0.008 m thick) out of the identical SurfaceTool. Both use the identical bar - 0.0630 x 0.0294 x 0.016 m - and the identical two colours, because colour follows the symbol INDEX and both alphabets receive the same indices from the same partition of [0,1). THE ENTIRE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE TWO FRAMES IS 90 DEGREES OF ROTATION APPLIED TO TWO OBJECTS: plaque 1 carries the bar at +45 against 0, plaque 2 at -45 against +90. Every other pair in the column changes either the plaque count (primitives 4, csg_tree 9, parametric 9 against these 2) or the mark's SHAPE - blocks swaps the bar for a 0.063 m plate and a 0.021 m speck, voxel swaps it for a 0.056 m cube and for NOTHING, and voxel's cube alone contributes 0.00176 m2 of screen from its side face, which is already 86 percent of this whole prediction.

THE NUMBER, computed on a polygon-clipping replica rather than by the W^2/sin(theta) approximation. Each bar has area 0.06300 x 0.02940 = 0.00185220 m2. Two congruent rectangles sharing a centre and crossing at 45 degrees intersect in 0.00120375 m2 (the closed-form approximation gives 0.00122239, 1.5 percent high). A rotation from -45 to +90 is a crossing angle of 135 degrees, which is 45 degrees modulo 180, so it is the same figure. Symmetric difference per plaque is 2 x (0.00185220 - 0.00120375) = 0.00129690 m2, and over two plaques 0.00259381 m2.

Camera is capture_config_sweep's: FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, 760 x 760, framing 0.60 on the AABB - which is the FRAME at 0.96 x 0.96 x 0.16, diagonal 1.36704 m, so the frame is 1.36704 x 1.9 x 0.60 = 1.5584 m across in every cell and the subject stands 1.09466 / 1.5584 = 70.9 percent of it, well clear of the edge. Screen basis at that standpoint: x-hat -> (0.8139, 0.1494), y-hat -> (0, 0.9664), z-hat -> (0.5810, 0.2093). The bars lie in the xy plane, which projects at |x-hat x y-hat| = 0.7866 - the reason the panel is vertical, since the same patch lying flat would project at 0.0835. Changed screen area = 0.00259381 x 0.7866 = 0.00204029 m2.

The subject box is the frame: 0.96 x 0.8139 + 0.16 x 0.5810 = 0.87430 m wide by 0.96 x 0.1494 + 0.96 x 0.9664 + 0.16 x 0.2093 = 1.10466 m tall = 0.96581 m2. So the changed area is 0.2113 percent of the subject box. The critic crops to the union of the two frames' subject boxes - identical here, because the frame is - neutralises each frame's own corner, greys, resizes to 160 x 160 = 25600 px, and takes the mean of the hottest 5 percent = 1280 px. 0.2113 percent of 25600 is 54.1 changed pixels, FAR FEWER than the 1280-pixel window, so THE WINDOW DOES NOT FILL AND THE NUMBER IS SET BY DILUTION, NOT BY CONTRAST. That is the opposite regime from most predictions in this corpus and it is why the figure is small.

Contrast on the pixels that do change: the bar covers plaque in one frame and not the other. Plaque 1 carries the warm symbol at luminance 0.694 against plaque 0.310, a separation of 0.384 = 38.4 percent; plaque 2 carries the cool symbol at 0.493, a separation of 0.183 = 18.3 percent. Equal areas, so the mean is 28.4 percent. Focus = (54.1 x 28.4 + 1225.9 x 0.3) / 1280 = 1.485 percent, where 0.3 is render noise on identical geometry. Applying the lighting-and-tonemap compression the substance_room replica measured at 0.77 gives 1.144. The bars' side faces are 0.016 m deep and they move too; that is worth roughly a fifth more changed area and is not in the polygon figure, so 1.144 x 1.2 = 1.372. Registered at 1.4.

THE PREDICTION IS A FLOOR, NOT A FORECAST. The replica has one key, flat shading, no shadows, no AO, no antialiasing, and every prior prediction in this corpus under-read by 1.5x to 6.7x, so the sweep should land somewhere between 2 and 9 percent. IF IT COMES BACK BELOW 1.4 ON THE NAMED PAIR, STOP AND INVESTIGATE THE HARNESS BEFORE THE DESIGN: (a) tools/check_dna_declarations.py, because a value the code cannot reach falls back to `diagonals` and prints two identical tiles - and `diagonals` IS the default, so this pair fails silently to zero rather than to something obviously wrong; (b) _rejects.json, because both exports are String enums and Object.set() on a typed property of the wrong type is refused in SILENCE; (c) whether the sheet was captured with --max=21, because at build_dna_gallery's default cap of 16 the 7 x 3 cross product is trimmed from the tail of the LATER axis and `reading` collapses to [field, glyphs], which deletes the entire reach shelf and therefore the whole refutation.

NOTHING IN THIS PREDICTION DEPENDS ON A DRAW. The glyphs reading does not consume the stream at all - it enumerates the vocabulary - so both frames are the same in every seed, and the 1.4 percent is a consequence of the two rotations and the two plaque positions alone.

dna.designed_nulls_why:
NONE, AND THAT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. Every one of the twenty-one cells is distinct by construction, and the reason is that the alphabet is the ONLY thing that varies while every alphabet's marks are different objects. The brief named three candidate mechanisms and this build supplies none of them, checked one at a time.

  SHARED SYMBOLS. No two of the seven alphabets share a mark. The bar at +45 is not the bar at 0; the filled cell is not the cube (0.063 m flat plate against a 0.056 m solid cube, and the cube's side face alone is 0.00176 m2 of screen); the triangle is not the ribbon. The four two-symbol alphabets share their PLAQUE ROW in the glyphs reading and their SHELF LAYOUT in the reach reading - same positions, same count, same 16 plaques - but never a mark, which is precisely why diagonals-against-orthogonals is the pre-registered closest pair rather than a null.

  A STRICT SUBSET. THIS ONE ALMOST EXISTS AND THE CODE DESTROYS IT, which is the interesting part. csg_tree's solids are {sphere, box, cylinder} and primitives' are {sphere, box, cylinder, torus} - a strict subset in the SOURCE, and if csg_tree drew its solids its glyphs row would be primitives' row with the torus removed and several cells would collapse. It does not draw them: add_primitive_to_surface ignores the primitive name entirely and emits one triangle, so the subset relation is real in create_csg_genome and invisible in every pixel. A null that the declaration predicts and the renderer refuses is the same fault this bench is about, one level up.

  A ONE-SYMBOL ALPHABET'S SINGLE OBJECT. There is no one-symbol alphabet here, because there is no one-symbol alphabet in the sources - `voxel`, the brief's candidate, turned out to be {cube, void}. Its glyphs row is two plaques with one mark, which is unique in the sheet and not shared with anything.

So none is registered. The alternative was to force one - to size voxel's cube at 0.063 to match blocks' plate, or to give two alphabets a common mark - and every version of that would have been a null manufactured for the ledger rather than found in the code. Across waves 14-19 sixty-one of sixty-one registered nulls held; a sixty-second bought by editing a constant would be worth less than the four sentences above. WHAT TO WATCH INSTEAD: if any pair in the glyphs column comes back UNDER 0.5 percent, that is not a null, it is a value falling back to the default, and _rejects.json is the first place to look.
dna.fixture_why: The bench can stand all seven alphabets in a row (layout=ladder, 1.10 m pitch, about 7.6 m wide) but the SWEEP must see one at a time: capture_config_sweep unions the AABB across a spec's variants, so a seven-wide row in the same spec would frame every single cell against seven and a half metres and photograph a 0.0294 m bar as a hair. layout is an export and not an axis, and it ships at single, so the fixture is a belt over braces. WHAT IS NOT FIXTURED, AND WHY NOTHING ELSE NEEDS TO BE: there is no clock and no unseeded draw here. All 144 numbers come from one RandomNumberGenerator seeded at RULE_SEED 20260816 in _draw_stream, called once per rebuild before any alphabet is consulted; there is no _process, no Timer, no tween, no FastNoiseLite and deliberately no NoiseTexture2D, which bakes on a worker thread and would let the shutter catch an unbaked map. That matters more here than usual, because BOTH sources are unphotographable twice. GeneticProgramming rolls every genome off the GLOBAL stream Godot randomises at boot - its own header says two boots of the same map produced twenty entirely different creatures and any two frames differed by 100 percent no matter what changed - and its population_seed ships at -1, meaning no seed call is made at all; one of its two registry names fixtures 20260802 and the other fixtures nothing. ten_print_textile ships weave_seed 0, which is `_rng.randomize()`, plus a _process that scrolls the whole bolt every 0.18 s and weaves a fresh row at the top, so it needs a fixture of {weave_seed: 7, weaving: false} to hold still. Between them the family is a random cloth on a moving loom and a random population on a global stream. This bench has no time-domain export to refuse and no unseeded draw to pin.
dna.kin: The three names are two artifacts and both are the kin, and the relation is unusually direct because ten_print_textile borrowed this bench's word from GeneticProgramming on purpose - its registry vocabulary_note says so in as many words. GeneticProgramming is a 30 m field of twenty evolving bodies whose truth line is that evolution does not design, it accumulates accidents that happen to survive; `alphabet` there is the one export its own promotion note calls the deepest claim in genetic programming - evolution cannot find what its representation cannot express - and this bench is that sentence tested rather than asserted, because the representation is held up beside its own reachable set. ten_print_textile is a 1.16 x 1.8 m loom whose truth line is that a generative rule is a pattern production never finishes printing; `alphabet` there is the two glyphs of a one-line BASIC program, and this bench is the room where its three two-symbol vocabularies finally stand beside a nine-symbol one and a continuous one at the same scale. A room holding this bench beside either source says the same sentence twice about the RULE and for the first time about the SYMBOL SET; a room holding it beside both is the comparison the two of them describe in their own notes and cannot perform, because one is a 30 m population grid on an unseeded global stream and the other is a scrolling bolt of cloth. ON THE VALUE SIDE this is the corpus's most lopsided shared vocabulary: one word, two members, seven values, and NOT ONE value in common between the two lists. cohort_bench's family agreed on all five words; this one agrees on the word and on nothing else, which is why the union had to be built rather than picked.
declines: THE BRIEF'S ARGUMENT, corrected from the code in three places, and the corrections are the pass. (a) ten_print_textile's `alphabet` axis does NOT vary alphabet size - all three of its values are two-symbol alphabets, and the member is already running the experiment the brief proposed. (b) `voxel` is not one cube; create_voxel_genome's `randf() < 0.3` makes it {cube, void} and the void is the reason a cube alphabet spans 2^512 bodies. (c) `csg_tree` is not four boolean operations on solids with a vastly larger reachable set; it is nine declared gene kinds that all render as one flat triangle, so its reach is ONE. The brief's headline - that alphabet size does not predict expressiveness - survives all three corrections and is in fact much better supported by the code than by the guess, because the counter-example runs in both directions at once.

THE TWO TEXTILE COLOURS AS THE SOURCE SETS THEM. ten_print_textile builds Color.from_hsv(0.07, 0.6, 0.95) and from_hsv(0.58, 0.6, 0.95) - Rec.709 luminance 0.672 and 0.633, THIRTY-NINE THOUSANDTHS APART. Its two symbols are a near-isoluminant pair, which is exactly the trap this project's notes warn about: the critic measures luminance by default and a pair separated only by hue reads as a twin in greyscale. The hues are kept and the VALUES are pushed apart - 0.98 and 0.74 - giving 0.694 and 0.493, a separation of 0.201. This does not change any measured pair in the sheet, because colour here follows the symbol INDEX and both members of the pre-registered pair receive the same indices; it changes only whether a human reading the gallery can see which mark is which. The source's own randf() hue jitter of +-0.05 is dropped outright, because it would be a 145th draw and the rule allows exactly 144.

THE SOURCE'S OTHER EIGHT PARAMETRIC PARAMETERS AS DRAWS. create_parametric_genome rolls nine numbers per genome - three frequencies, three amplitudes, three phases. The rule here spends exactly ONE number per cell, so eight of the nine are pinned at the midpoints of the source's own randf_range calls (amp 1.25 of 0.5..2.0, freq 1.75 of 0.5..3.0) and the phase carries the draw. Rolling all nine would have given parametric nine times the randomness of every other alphabet and made its saturated reach shelf a fact about the draw budget rather than about the alphabet. THE SAME DECISION, MADE THE SAME WAY, for csg_tree's per-gene scale (randf_range(0.5, 2) on three axes, pinned to the cell fit) and for primitives' per-gene position, rotation and scale (pinned to zero rotation at the cell centre). One draw per cell is the rule and the rule is the thing that must be identical.

GENOME COUNT AS PART OF THE ALPHABET. create_primitive_genome builds `randi() % genome_complexity + 3` genes, that is 3 to 10; create_csg_genome builds 2 to 5; parametric and voxel build exactly one gene each. So in the source the alphabets differ in HOW MANY SYMBOLS A BODY GETS as well as in which symbols exist, and a body of ten primitives against a body of one parametric surface is not a comparison of alphabets at all. Every alphabet here gets exactly 144 symbols. That is a real departure from all four GP branches and it is the departure that makes the sheet mean anything.

THE FIFTH GP BRANCH, L_System. genome_type 4 exists in the export enum and in every match block, and it is NOT in the declared axis - GeneticProgramming's own promotion note explains why at length and the reason is a live bug: interpret_lsystem rotates the heading with `direction.rotated(Vector3.UP, angle)` while the heading IS Vector3.UP, which is a no-op, so the turtle never turns and create_branch_segment's `look_at(end, Vector3.UP)` then errors once per segment on a look direction parallel to its up vector. At 4 iterations of "FF+[+F-F-F]-[-F+F+F]" that is up to 4096 cylinders per genome. It is the value this bench most wanted - a genome that is a SENTENCE rather than a bag of parts is the sharpest possible contrast to a bag of parts, and it is the one alphabet in the family whose symbols COMPOSE rather than merely occur. It is excluded for the same reason its own member excluded it: a repair, not a value. It is also the reason this bench's rule is i.i.d. per cell and cannot express grammar at all, which is `reach`'s second blind spot after censoring.

A GRAMMAR, which is what an L-system would have needed and what the artifact's name half-promises. The rule here is 10 PRINT's rule - one uniform draw per cell, independent of every neighbour - and it is chosen because it is the ONE rule both sources actually run: create_random_gene, create_voxel_genome and _weave_row are all i.i.d. draws from a flat distribution. A production rule with context would have been a better test of expressiveness and a worse test of ALPHABET, because the reachable set would then depend on the rule as much as on the symbols and no cell in the sheet could be attributed to one or the other. The name is `alphabet_grammar` because the grammar is the constant and the alphabet is the variable; if that reads as a promise of production rules it is a promise this file does not keep, and the reason is here rather than hidden.

THE 2 x 2 NEIGHBOURHOOD AS THE REACH KEY, over the two obvious alternatives. A single cell would have given the alphabet's size back verbatim - 2, 2, 2, 2, 4, 1, 121 - which measures nothing the glyphs row does not already show. A horizontal PAIR gives |A|^2, which is 4 for the two-symbol alphabets: a four-plaque shelf is under the blank floor and too coarse to separate anything. The 2 x 2 block gives |A|^4 = 16 for a two-symbol alphabet, which fills one and a half rows of an eleven-wide shelf, and 121 for the saturating cases, which fills it exactly. It is also the smallest window in which a MAZE differs from a DITHER, which is the distinction diagonals and blocks exist to make.

KEYING THE REACH BY THE DECLARED SYMBOL. If the block key were the symbol INDEX rather than the drawn mark, csg_tree would report about 120 distinct configurations out of 9^4 = 6561 and the shelf would say it is the second-widest alphabet in the sheet. That number would be true about create_csg_genome and false about every pixel. The key is what is drawn, which is the one decision this whole reading rests on, and it is why _mark_key returns a constant for all nine csg symbols and the exact float for parametric.

A HORIZONTAL FIELD, which is how GeneticProgramming lays out its population - visualize_population arranges phenotypes on the xz plane at 6.0 m spacing. At capture_config_sweep's standpoint (yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26) a horizontal plane projects at 0.0835 of its area and a vertical one in the xy plane at 0.7866, nine and a half times better, so a floor raster of 0.029 m bars would have photographed as a smear. The panel is vertical, which is ten_print_textile's geometry rather than GeneticProgramming's, and it is why the two sources' scales could not both be kept.

THE MEMBERS' SCALE. GeneticProgramming measures 29.96 x 6.18 x 23.33 m and ten_print_textile 1.16 x 1.8 x 0.1 m - 29.96 against 1.80 on the long axis, a factor of 16.6 between two artifacts declaring the same axis, which is itself worth recording. Everything here is rebuilt at 0.84 m of field with the RATIOS preserved and the ratios named above: 0.9 of the cell for the bar's length and for every primitive's extent, 0.42 for the bar's thickness, 0.3 for the speck, 0.8 for the voxel cube (BoxMesh 0.4 on a 0.5 pitch), 0.3/1.4 and 0.7/1.4 for the torus. Not one absolute number is shared with either source. The one thing that could not be inherited is the seed, because neither source has one to inherit - GeneticProgramming ships population_seed = -1 and ten_print_textile ships weave_seed = 0, and both of those mean "do not seed".
dna.sweep_note: THE FULL SHEET NEEDS --max=21 AND THE COST OF GETTING IT WRONG IS THE ENTIRE REFUTATION. `alphabet` is declared first and is never trimmed; `reading` is second, and build_dna_gallery trims the LATER axis from the tail until the cross product fits its cap. At the current default of 16 the 7 x 3 sheet renders as 7 x 2 = field and glyphs, which deletes the reach shelf - so the sheet would show seven fields and seven vocabulary rows, would rank csg_tree as the largest alphabet in the family with nine plaques, and would have no way at all to say that its reach is one. That is a finished-looking sheet of fourteen distinct tiles making exactly the claim this artifact exists to refute. At --max=14 it renders 7 x 2 as well; at --max=7 it collapses to `field` alone. Only 21 carries the experiment. The pre-registered pair lives in the glyphs column and survives any cap of 14 or more; the argument does not.
